rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Each listed source carries a freshness STAMP, not just a to-do.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L111's stamp for Item 4's lineage reads: '`[checked:2026-08-30 result:OK due:none]` `supplementary/workflow-composition-lineages.md:cognition-multi-agents-working` — [delegated stamp] Item 4's single-writer shape; the dated live check (currently 2026-05-25, due 2026-11-25) is owned by the supplementary. `due:none`, a delegation does not expire.' Two problems, both grounded: (1) '[delegated stamp]' is not a label §1 defines, and 'a delegation does not expire' is not one of §11a's three sanctioned due:none categories (§2a durable account / named theory construct / maintainer-ATTESTED) — this invents a fourth. (2) The restated fact is already wrong: I grepped the actual supplementary (`curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/workflow-composition-lineages.md:185`) and its `cognition-multi-agents-working` stamp reads `[checked:2026-05-25 result:OK due:2026-10-22]` — due 2026-10-22, not 2026-11-25 as claimed here. Harm: this is the exact failure §11a's own 2026-08-30 compounded lesson (`compounded/2026-08-30-research_claims-a-stamp-records-its-own-check.md`, dated the SAME DAY as this stamp's checked-date) was written to name — 'a stamp whose evidence is prose in another file inherits that file's edits... the claim loses its evidence with nothing to notice.' Here the drift has already happened: the pointed-at fact is stale/wrong at the moment of writing, not hypothetically later. Harm is muted for the STUDENT (body doesn't attribute Item 4 to Cognition/Yan at all, per the maintainer's own note two lines up), but the maintainer-block verification-debt record itself is now inaccurate, which is exactly what this section exists to prevent for whoever runs the pre-cohort pass.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Per §11a's prescribed fix, restate the check inline (what Yan's post says, when it was verified) instead of pointing at the supplementary's due date; if a genuine 'delegated to another file's freshness cycle' shape is wanted, that's a rule-amendment question for the maintainer (§11a's due:none enum doesn't currently have a slot for it), not a citing-file invention. At minimum, correct 2026-11-25 to the supplementary's actual 2026-10-22 today.
